analysis.title: USA: Fed Governor Waller Says He Anticipates "Additional Hikes"
key_insights: Fed Governor Waller suggested he likely expects two additional rate hikes to be appropriate, which would raise the funds rate to 4.25-4.50%.

Waller said that if data continue to come in as expected he anticipates additional hikes to support a timelier return of inflation to 2%, with flexibility on timing. The hikes do not need to come at consecutive meetings.

Waller cited three forces undermining his faith that inflation is progressing toward 2%: no resolution to the Middle East conflict, signs the AI buildout is raising high-tech consumer prices, and the risk of new tariffs.

Waller said his view changed on a preponderance of evidence over several months that risks had shifted, reflecting a strengthened labor market and persistent inflationary forces. He said core inflation is not showing sufficient progress.

Waller endorsed the Fed's current communication approach, including the dot plot in the SEP, as having the flavor of forward guidance but not being forward guidance. GS reads this as a sign he would likely oppose eliminating the SEP, which is under review by task forces.
GS continues to expect one additional 25bp hike in December, which would raise the funds rate to 4-4.25%, and has lowered its probability that the FOMC could pass on a December hike.
GS says Waller's speech is a hawkish shift relative to his earlier emphasis on the three-month annualized rate of core PCE inflation, which is now 2.0%.
GS expects that by March the inflation data will have improved enough to convince most of the FOMC that additional hikes are unnecessary.
Williams and Jefferson comments last week pointed toward skipping a hike in October, in line with Waller's message.

macro_indicators.reading: One additional 25bp hike in December, to 4-4.25%
macro_indicators.interpretation: GS base case is a single further hike, with a lower probability of the FOMC passing in December after Waller's remarks.

macro_indicators.indicator: Fed funds rate (implied by Waller's two hikes)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Two more hikes, as Waller suggested he likely expects, would take the funds rate to this range.
Core PCE momentum is at the 2% target on a three-month basis. Waller's hawkish shift came despite this reading.

macro_indicators.reading: Eight participants expect rates 50bp higher at end-2027 than today
macro_indicators.interpretation: Waller cited this, and noted markets read it as the Committee likely raising the policy rate 50bp in the coming months.

risk_factors: Unresolved Middle East conflict keeping inflation pressures elevated.
AI buildout raising consumer prices for high-tech goods.
Strengthened labor market and persistent inflationary forces.
geopolitical: Waller cited the lack of a resolution to the Middle East conflict as a reason inflation progress is in doubt.
Waller cited the risk of new tariffs as undermining confidence that inflation is returning to 2%.

tension_points.bull_case: Waller expects two more hikes, with timing flexible and not necessarily at consecutive meetings, because core inflation is not showing sufficient progress and the labor market has strengthened.
tension_points.bear_case: Three-month annualized core PCE is 2.0%, and GS expects inflation data to improve enough by March to convince most of the FOMC that further hikes are unnecessary. Williams and Jefferson pointed toward skipping a hike in October.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Inflation data improving enough by March to convince most of the FOMC that additional hikes are unnecessary.
